macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks slip as bond selloff and higher yields pressure markets
items.summary: Major U.S. indexes were lower in early trading, with the S&P 500 down 0.61% and the Dow down 0.21% as a global bond-market rout weighed on risk assets. Reuters-based market coverage also noted that major U.S. indexes were headed for a third straight session in the red.

items.title: Treasury yields ease ahead of Fed minutes after recent surge
items.summary: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield eased toward 4.7% and the 30-year yield pulled back after hitting a 19-year high above 5.33% on Tuesday. Markets are waiting for the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes for more clues on the policy outlook.

items.title: Fed minutes and broader central-bank signals dominate macro focus
items.summary: The upcoming FOMC minutes are the key U.S. policy event in focus, with traders also watching comments from ECB President Christine Lagarde and other central-bank developments. Persistent moves in global government bond yields are keeping pressure on equities and rate-sensitive assets.

items.title: UK inflation rises to 2.9%, reinforcing rate concerns
items.summary: UK annual inflation accelerated to 2.9% in July from 2.6% in June, driven mainly by higher energy bills and matching analyst expectations. Coverage noted this has increased pressure on the Bank of England, which is still expected to keep rates unchanged for the rest of the year.

items.title: Global borrowing costs hit fresh highs amid inflation and fiscal worries
items.summary: Long-term government borrowing costs in the U.S., UK, Germany and Japan climbed to fresh highs as investors focused on inflation, heavy debt issuance and fiscal concerns. Reuters-linked market news also highlighted pressure from oil and AI-related developments.

items.title: U.S. retail sales fall sharply, signaling softer consumer demand
items.summary: U.S. retail sales fell 0.6% in July from the prior month, the steepest monthly drop since May 2025. The weaker consumer data adds to concerns about growth as markets digest higher yields and tighter financial conditions.

items.title: U.S. fiscal deficit widens sharply in July
items.summary: The U.S. fiscal deficit jumped to $432.3 billion in July, the highest monthly total since March 2021, pushing the year-to-date shortfall to nearly $1.8 trillion. The larger deficit has been cited as one factor contributing to recent pressure on Treasury markets.

items.title: Germany says economy is on track to shrink for a second straight year
items.summary: Germany's government said its economy is on track to contract for a second consecutive year, underscoring renewed weakness in Europe’s growth outlook. European equity indices were lower in the latest market snapshot, including the CAC 40 and FTSE MIB.

items.title: European stocks decline as bond yields and risk aversion rise
items.summary: The CAC 40, STOXX Europe 50, FTSE MIB and IBEX 35 were all lower in the latest market data, reflecting broader pressure from rising yields and cautious risk appetite. Market coverage also pointed to a stronger U.S. dollar and firmer crude oil prices.

items.title: Retail and consumer-focused companies in focus as earnings season continues
items.summary: Market commentary says investors are awaiting quarterly reports from large retailers to gauge U.S. consumer spending strength, while other reports note chip stocks were under pressure as inflation fears returned. No single company announcement dominated the available headlines.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades around $64K–$65K after a volatile 24 hours
items.summary: Bitcoin’s latest moves were mixed, with reports showing it rebounding to about $64,000 after an AI-led selloff, then trading near $64,700 as softer U.S. inflation eased rate-hike concerns. Other market snapshots showed BTC around $64,421 to $64,688, indicating a broadly resilient but choppy session.

items.title: SEC proposes new crypto framework with capital-raising exemptions
items.summary: The U.S. SEC unveiled a new proposal called “Regulation Crypto Assets,” aiming to give token issuers clearer paths to raise capital under federal securities laws. The framework includes exemptions for offerings up to $5 million over four years and up to $75 million every 12 months.

items.title: FASB moves to treat some stablecoins as cash equivalents
items.summary: The U.S. Financial Accounting Standards Board proposed conditions under which certain stablecoins could be classified as cash equivalents. Market commentary said the accounting shift could matter for firms holding or using stablecoins in treasury and payments workflows.

items.title: Singapore court freezes S$75 million in Bitcoin and USDC
items.summary: A Singapore court reportedly froze roughly S$75 million in Bitcoin and USDC amid a transfer dispute. The case adds to a steady stream of legal actions involving disputed crypto custody and on-chain asset transfers.

items.title: Nexo launches regulated crypto-backed credit lines in Australia
items.summary: Nexo announced regulated crypto-backed Credit Lines in Australia, expanding its lending products into a new jurisdiction. The launch was highlighted as part of a broader trend toward regulated crypto financial services.

items.title: Visa seeks stablecoin partner across four markets
items.summary: Visa is reportedly looking for a stablecoin partner in four markets, signaling continued interest from major payment networks in blockchain-based settlement and cross-border payment infrastructure. The move comes alongside broader industry efforts to integrate stablecoins into mainstream payments.

items.title: MoonPay adds Cash App Pay for U.S. crypto purchases
items.summary: MoonPay expanded payment options by adding Cash App Pay for U.S. customers buying crypto. The integration is another step toward lowering friction for retail crypto onboarding.

items.title: Sei begins phased Eidos upgrade targeting 200,000 TPS
items.summary: Sei started a phased Eidos upgrade designed to prepare the network for throughput of up to 200,000 transactions per second. The development underscores ongoing competition among blockchain projects to scale performance.

items.title: Binance says it stopped a $1.2 million DAO governance attack
items.summary: Binance reported that it halted a DAO governance attack involving about $1.2 million. The incident highlights continued security risks in decentralized governance and treasury systems.

items.title: Maya Protocol suffers exploit and halts operations
items.summary: Maya Protocol reportedly paused after an attacker exploited six chained bugs and drained about $1.7 million from the decentralized liquidity protocol. The incident makes it one of the day’s notable DeFi security events.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI pauses frontier training after cyber risk concerns
items.summary: OpenAI has paused reinforcement-learning training on its newest models for two weeks after preliminary evidence suggested its upcoming Astra model could reach a critical cybersecurity threshold under the company’s Preparedness Framework. The move reflects growing concern about frontier-model security and alignment during advanced training.[3][17]
items.source: The AI Rankings / Channel News Asia

items.title: Nvidia backs OpenAI’s huge Ohio data center deal
items.summary: OpenAI has locked in a lease for a large Ohio data center project with backing from Nvidia, and reports say Nvidia may be guaranteeing land, power, and buildout for a site valued at up to $105 billion. The announcement underscores how rapidly AI infrastructure spending is expanding.[1][9]
items.source: The Wall Street Journal / South China Morning Post

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with stronger safety controls
items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT for Teens, adding Study Mode, parental controls, and safety features designed to limit high-risk conversations about self-harm, eating disorders, violence, and other sensitive topics. The release highlights a broader industry push toward age-specific guardrails and safer consumer AI products.[15][18]

items.title: Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash with lower pricing
items.summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, a model positioned for coding and agent workflows, and appears to be pricing it aggressively relative to prior offerings. The release adds pressure in the fast-moving competition over capable but cheaper frontier models.[7][15]

items.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3 with long context and cybersecurity claims
items.summary: Chinese AI company Z.ai released GLM-5.3, a reasoning model with a 1M-token context window and pricing that undercuts many competitors. The model’s cyber-related performance claims have drawn attention because they appear to be partially supported by real vulnerability databases.[5][10][16]

items.title: OpenAI announces support for democratic oversight bodies
items.summary: OpenAI announced a planned initiative to help democratic government oversight bodies build expertise and tools for reviewing AI use in national security, with $5 million in training, technical support, and credits over the next year. The move suggests increasing emphasis on institutional governance around frontier AI.[5]

items.title: Cerebras unveils CS-4 rack-scale AI system
items.summary: Cerebras announced the CS-4, a rack-scale AI system built around its WSE-Turbo wafers, claiming major gains in inference speed and throughput per watt versus its previous generation. The launch adds to competition in specialized AI hardware and inference infrastructure.[5]

items.title: Etched raises $700 million as AI chip investment accelerates
items.summary: Inference-chip startup Etched reportedly raised $700 million at a $21 billion valuation, led by Jane Street after the firm tested and bought the hardware during diligence. The deal reflects continued investor appetite for AI infrastructure and custom silicon.[13][18]

items.title: Stripe reportedly acquires OpenRouter in a major AI infrastructure deal
items.summary: Reports say Stripe has finalized a deal to buy AI gateway startup OpenRouter for more than $7 billion. If confirmed, the acquisition would signal that AI model-routing and access infrastructure have become strategically valuable.[3]

items.title: AI spending and physical-AI funding continue to surge
items.summary: Recent reporting says venture funding in physical AI reached $47.4 billion across 521 deals in the first half of 2026, up sharply from the same period last year. Broader coverage also points to rising corporate AI spending even as near-term earnings impact remains limited.[18][7]

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple unveils new EU business terms for apps
items.summary: Apple announced updated App Store and business terms for the European Union starting October 1, including a new 5% Core Technology Commission and revised commission tiers. The move is aimed at resolving disputes with the European Commission.

items.title: Fairphone launches repairable Fairphone 6+ in the U.S.
items.summary: Dutch company Fairphone has launched its $650 flagship repairable phone in the U.S. and said it plans to release new phone generations every two years. The move expands the company’s presence beyond its core European market.

items.title: Nvidia backs massive OpenAI Ohio data center project
items.summary: Nvidia is reportedly providing $105 billion in financing toward OpenAI's planned Ohio data center, which would become one of the largest in the world. The project underscores continued investment in large-scale tech infrastructure.

items.title: Groq raises $350 million as it expands beyond chips
items.summary: Groq reportedly raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation while pivoting toward a neocloud business and expanding its Nvidia-powered data center footprint. The funding highlights continued capital flow into infrastructure-heavy tech businesses.

items.title: Cerebras launches new server chip and system
items.summary: Cerebras has launched a new server chip and system designed to accelerate chatbot workloads. The release adds another notable hardware development in the semiconductor and enterprise systems market.

items.title: Discord suspends livestreams in Brazil
items.summary: Discord said it has halted livestreaming in Brazil after regulators cited child safety failures. The move follows increased scrutiny of platform safety and moderation practices.

items.title: China recaptures first stage of a rocket on land for the first time
items.summary: China successfully recovered the first stage of a rocket on land, a milestone for its space program. The achievement signals progress in reusable launch technology.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a teen-focused version of ChatGPT with stronger protections for users ages 13 to 17, including content restrictions around self-harm and sexual content. This is one of the main consumer product launches in the past day, though it is AI-specific.
